global_rules.rule: No burned-in captions or subtitles, in any video, long or Short. Ship the .srt file instead.
global_rules.why: Owner rule, flagged repeatedly. The engine only draws captions if a spec sets burn_captions, and none may.

global_rules.rule: Every subcontinent name (first and last) and Indian place name is written in Devanagari in the narration.
global_rules.why: The voice (ElevenLabs Ruhaan) mispronounces Latin spellings. voice_lint.py fails the build otherwise.

global_rules.rule: Say "Under nineteen", write "T-twenty", and spell every number out. No digits in the narration.
global_rules.why: Digits and short forms are misread, especially next to Devanagari.

global_rules.rule: Hook in two seconds: the key number or claim is on screen before anything else.
global_rules.why: Retention drops fastest in the first seconds, especially on Shorts.

global_rules.rule: No broadcast footage, player photos, team or league logos, or likeness of a real person.
global_rules.why: Copyright and monetisation safety. Players are our illustrated avatars in team colours.

global_rules.rule: Every fact that can change is checked on the web; every headline number against an official source.
global_rules.why: Accuracy is the brand. Lessons: the Aaryavir debut figure, the Cricsheet gaps, one Rashid wicket.

global_rules.rule: Every spec carries sources[], including how the data was filtered.
global_rules.why: Goes into the description, and lets us defend any number.

global_rules.rule: Label illustrative visuals (field plans, replays) as illustrative.
global_rules.why: Honesty about what is drawn from data and what is a reconstruction.

global_rules.rule: Write for the ear: short sentences, a comma wherever a narrator would breathe.
global_rules.why: Pauses come from punctuation; long runs sound rushed.

global_rules.rule: YouTube titles: `<Team A> vs <Team B> - <match label> <type> | <hook>`, keywords first, 75 characters or fewer, "vs" and full team names; series episodes carry the series and number (`<Question>? | Did You Know Ep 2 #Shorts`, Shorts add #Shorts, title case, no emoji); description starts with the same keywords and ends with hashtags.
global_rules.why: Search and suggested traffic: people search the fixture and match number. Full pattern list in CLAUDE.md (YouTube naming); rename an uploaded video by changing the spec and running publish/retitle.py.

global_rules.rule: Vary the venue, the camera and the poses from scene to scene; use synthesised sound effects.
global_rules.why: Keeps a faceless channel from looking the same every time.

global_rules.rule: No number goes into a video unless two independent sources agree (dataops/verify.py): a single-source number must be said as "in our archive". A claim that is UNVERIFIED or in CONFLICT blocks the build and the upload.
global_rules.why: Credibility first (owner rule, Nov 2026). Specs with provenance_required are gated in engine.py and publish/youtube.py.

global_rules.rule: Never make a "first / only / never / record" claim, or a career total, from Cricsheet alone. It is a partial sample (no Tests/ODIs before 2001-02, gaps in recent T20Is). Win probabilities are labelled "our model".
global_rules.why: Lessons: the Vaas three-wickets-in-an-over error, Kohli's missing 122*. Totals and records come from Tier A (Cricinfo, ICC, boards).

global_rules.rule: No on-screen source or footer lines in any video (never set "foot" on a scene). Credit sources only in the YouTube description and the spec's sources[].
global_rules.why: Owner rule, flagged repeatedly. Sources stay verifiable without cluttering the frame.

global_rules.rule: Every vertical video ships in two versions: the YouTube Short (end card "Want the full breakdown? Subscribe") and the Instagram version (end card "Full breakdown on YouTube, LINK IN BIO"), each with its own cover and caption. Reels carry their own reel_cta; Lab-style stories also get a no-avatar vertical Lab Reel.
global_rules.why: Instagram is posted by hand from the _IG files; the end cards send each audience to the right place.

global_rules.rule: Everything new that is generated goes to Drive and the tracker in the same session, even if it is not uploaded. Upload to YouTube only when the owner asks (default private); after an upload set Status=Posted and the link.
global_rules.why: Owner rule: nothing built should exist only on one machine, and nothing goes public without a go-ahead. Test renders are the exception.

global_rules.rule: Secrets (API keys, tokens) come only from environment variables and are never written to a file, spec, commit or log.
global_rules.why: The repository is public to collaborators and CI; a leaked key is the one mistake that cannot be undone.

formats.name: The Replay Room
formats.pitch: What really happened in the match, who decided it and why: from every ball's line, length, shot, control and direction.
formats.trigger: An India international finishes. Post the long video within 24 hours, Shorts the same day.
formats.data: Cricinfo + Cricbuzz match captures (tools/ttm-capture) for ODIs and Tests; Sportmonks for T20Is and the IPL. Cross-checked over by over and against the official scorecard.
formats.look: Lab charts for the numbers, Tactics Board for field plans, stadium-stage replays with the illustrated players for key shots.
beats: Cold open: the number that explains the match (0–2 s)
The turning point: control and run rate across all 50 overs, the phase where it was won
The innings that decided it: told ball by ball, with false shots and dropped catches marked
The hidden hero: the player the scorecard undersells (the luck meter: false shots drawn vs wickets)
The plan: where the field was, where the runs went
What if: the runs scored after each drop
Verdict and what it means for the next match
visuals: Wagon wheel that builds shot by shot
Pitch map of line and length
Innings timeline with false shots and drops
Illustrated replays: real shot direction and length
rules: Only our own graphics. Never copy Cricinfo or Cricbuzz charts, images or commentary text.
Cricbuzz notes are leads: verify each one against the ball data before it is said.
Credit "ball-by-ball data: ESPNcricinfo, Cricbuzz" in the description sources.
Label replays "Illustrated from ball-tracking data".
Use "in control" / "not in control" for the shot-control field; don't invent new metrics without explaining them on screen.
Win probability shown is our model (Cricsheet 50-over ODIs); label it "our model" and say when matches were decided by DLS.
Drop counts and runs-after-drops taken from Cricbuzz alone are single-source: say "in our archive".

formats.name: Data Stories
formats.tag: One question, answered from the numbers
formats.pitch: A long data story on one question (a series, a player, a trend, a trade), built from ball-by-ball data and checked against official records, with a Short and Instagram cuts.
formats.length: Long (Ep 12: about 3 min) + a Short (about 1 min); Instagram Short, Reel and, for chart-led stories, a no-avatar Lab Reel
formats.trigger: A series ends, a milestone or debate revives a question, or a quiet week needs an evergreen explainer. Post within a few days.
formats.data: Sportmonks for IPL and T20Is; Cricsheet and the owner's Cricinfo/Cricbuzz captures for ODIs and Tests; official records for every headline number. Claims go through dataops/verify.py.
formats.look: Lab charts and stadium stage scenes, themed by the story; captions are never burned in (the .srt ships separately).
beats: The number that answers the question, on screen in two seconds
What the numbers show, one idea per scene
The check: a second source or a robustness test
The verdict and what to watch next
visuals: Lab charts built from the data
Illustrated stage scenes in team colours
On-screen caveat labels ("in our archive", "our model")
rules: Registered in publish/series.py (data) before its first build; episodes numbered in the title ("Data Story Ep 12").
Single-source numbers (for example drop counts from Cricbuzz) are said to be "in our archive".
A story is held when its key claim lacks a second source (Gambhir "Player vs Coach": the coach record).
Win probabilities are labelled "our model"; note DLS decisions where they matter.

formats.name: Myth or Data?
formats.pitch: Take something everyone says ("Kohli fails in knockouts") and settle it with the numbers, ending on a verdict stamp.
formats.length: Short 1–1.5 min; long 4–6 min when the evidence is rich
formats.trigger: A claim is trending: a commentator's line, a social-media debate, a milestone that revives an old argument. Post within 2–3 days.
formats.data: Sportmonks (IPL, T20Is), Cricsheet (Tests, ODIs; check completeness), official records.
formats.look: Theme "stadium": stage scenes with the illustrated player, poses per beat, the ball on shot moments, opponent avatar on versus beats.
beats: The claim, on screen in two seconds
The evidence, two or three numbers
Verdict stamp: busted / half true / confirmed
visuals: Stadium stage with venue matched to the real ground
Poses: walk, stance, drive, pull, celebrate, dejected
rules: Always end on the verdict stamp, so the series has a recognisable sign-off.
State the definition used (e.g. which matches count as knockouts).
Never present Cricsheet sums as career totals without checking the official record.

formats.name: The Lab
formats.pitch: A question only a model can answer: statistical twins, clusters, eras compared. Editorial-paper look, numbered episodes.
formats.trigger: Evergreen. Quiet weeks with no India cricket, end of a season, or when a player's season begs comparison.
formats.data: Sportmonks IPL 2013–2026 ball-by-ball (and captured internationals as they accumulate).
formats.look: Theme "lab": editorial paper, round tabs, lab_dots / lab_swarm / lab_radial / lab_rings / lab_units / lab_big. Title card with the player in a yellow disc and stat chips.
beats: Title card with the question and two stat chips
The checks (drop one measure, raise the bar, reverse search)
rules: Generate the spec from the analysis script and assert every claim in code.
Show the robustness checks on screen.
Count dismissals correctly (bowled rows carry no out_id).

formats.name: Stat Check
formats.pitch: "X or Y?" settled in rounds with a running scorecard and a final verdict.
formats.trigger: A debate between two players: trades, awards, selection, auction buzz, a rivalry in a live series.
formats.data: Sportmonks ball-by-ball; official records for career totals.
formats.look: Theme "lab" with the split-colour VS title card (both players in their kits, VS stamp), lab_vs and lab_score.
beats: Round 1…N: one measure each, league average for context
visuals: Split team-colour title with VS stamp
rules: Every round compares like with like (same phases, minimum balls).
Avoid any figure you can't reconcile with the official record (e.g. one Rashid wicket).

formats.name: Tactics Board
formats.pitch: How a match will be or was won: field plans, lengths, matchups, drawn on a tilted field.
formats.trigger: 1–3 days before a series or Test (preview), or after a match decided by a plan.
formats.data: Sportmonks for T20Is/IPL; captures and Cricsheet for ODIs/Tests; squad news from the web.
formats.look: "board" scenes (navy or cream), pucks, zones, ball paths, length band, mixed with Lab charts.
visuals: Tilted field with pucks and zones
rules: Label every field "Illustrative".
One label per zone (no stacked fielder labels).
Re-check squads and fitness the day before posting.

formats.name: What If?
formats.pitch: History rewritten with numbers: Bradman in the IPL, Sachin in the T20 era. Sepia film, back to colour at the end.
formats.trigger: Anniversaries, a legend in the news, or evergreen weekend slots.
formats.data: Career records, era-adjusted comparisons (z-scores), Sportmonks for the modern side.
formats.look: Stadium stage with "film": true (sepia), opening newspaper-style clipping (illustrative, no real masthead); last content scene in colour.
beats: The clipping: the moment history turned
Back to colour: what it would have meant
rules: Make the assumptions explicit on screen.
No real newspaper masthead or logo.

formats.name: Did You Know?
formats.tag: Rules, positions and the odd corners of cricket, explained
formats.pitch: One surprising or misunderstood thing about cricket per video: a rule, a position, something a player can or cannot do, a strange dismissal. It is explained, not just stated: what it is, where it is, why it exists, then the twist.
formats.length: Short 90-120 s, EXPLANATORY (the main product, 200-260 words) plus a 3-4 min long for bigger topics; each Short also ships as an Instagram version
formats.trigger: Evergreen, plus topical hooks: post the matching episode when the thing happens in a match (a Mankad, a timed-out, a handled-ball, a concussion substitute, a DLS reset, a super over).
formats.data: The Laws of Cricket (MCC, current code) for rules; the ICC Playing Conditions for format-specific rules (powerplays, DRS, over rates, concussion and impact substitutes); ESPNcricinfo / Wisden for history and first instances. A rule is quoted with its Law number and checked against two sources.
formats.look: The "plate" look (plate.py): cream field-guide plates with inked field plans, numbered figures and red stamps; scenes plate, plate_page and plate_list; series colour lime. Field plans are labelled Illustrative (right-handed batter, bowler at the top, off side on the right). The Law number is a stamp ("LAW 28.4").
beats: The question or the oddly-named thing on screen in two seconds ("Silly mid-off. Deep backward square leg. Third man.")
The short answer, then the idea built in steps (word one: the angle; word two: the distance)
The drawn example: a numbered field plan, one idea per plate
The Law in plain words, with its number and a stamp ("Law 28.4: two fielders behind the batting crease on the leg side, or it is a no ball")
The twist or the caveat most people miss (positions are loose labels; origins that nobody can document)
A verified real instance if there is one, or an invitation to try it in the comments; subscribe card
visuals: Plate: inked field with numbered figures (Fig. 1, Fig. 2) and a dashed ball path
Plate page: a Law quotation or a theory, with a margin note and a red stamp (UNPROVEN, LAW 28.4, CAPTAIN'S CALL)
Plate list: dated entries with dotted leaders
Illustrative labels on every field plan
rules: Every rule is checked against the Laws of Cricket and, for format rules, the ICC Playing Conditions: two sources, Law number in the description.

Say which version applies (Test / ODI / T20I / IPL) when rules differ, and which edition of the Laws. MCC published a 2026 edition (in force from October 2026): re-check that the clause number is unchanged before publishing. The MCC site and PDFs block automated reads; the ICC clause pages (icc-cricket.com, "Men's Test / ODI / T20I Match Clause 28: The Fielder") can be read.
Never present a real incident as the "first" or "only" without a Tier A source; an incident reported by one outlet (or reported inconsistently) is left out.
Our own drawings only; field plans labelled Illustrative.
Shorts explain, they do not just state: about 200-260 words, one idea built in steps, under three minutes so Reels and Shorts stay eligible for recommendation.
Title: `<Question or topic>? | Did You Know Ep N #Shorts`; description cites the Law number and both sources; episodes are registered in publish/series.py (didyouknow) before the first build.
Origins and etymologies nobody can document are said to be undocumented ("Why is it called third man?"), never filled with a theory presented as fact.
